notes: Get a SUBE card (from kiosks). The metro (Subte) and buses (colectivo) are cheap, and Uber/Cabify are safe. Ezeiza is 1 hour away; Aeroparque is in the city.
October-November: purple jacaranda trees in spring, the best season. December-February: 30-35°C and humid; locals are on holiday and the city is empty. March-May: autumn.
ARS inflation means prices change fast (ASSUMPTION: mid-2026). The 'dólar MEP' rate applied automatically on cards is good; Western Union for cash. The new 100 USD series is the one to bring.
Parrilla 30-60,000 ARS, empanada 2,000, coffee and medialuna 5,000, tango show 90,000+. Tip 10% in cash. Dinner is after 21:00.
Watch for pickpockets: off the main street in Caminito and at the Retiro bus terminal. Don't show your phone in the street. Bring your passport for Colonia.
Shared mate, dulce de leche, alfajores (Havanna), malbec; Recoleta's Sunday market.

stops.name: Plaza de Mayo
stops.tips: Casa Rosada (the pink palace, free tours at weekends), the Cathedral (Pope Francis's former church), and the Mothers of the Plaza de Mayo on Thursdays at 15:30.

stops.name: Café Tortoni
stops.tips: A café since 1858: order churros and hot chocolate. Expect a queue. On Avenida de Mayo.

stops.name: San Telmo Market
stops.tips: A market dating from 1897, with choripán (grilled sausage sandwich) and empanada stalls and antique dealers. On Sundays the Defensa street fair stretches over 10 blocks.

stops.name: Plaza Dorrego
stops.tips: Street tango on Sundays and antique shops.

stops.name: El Zanjón de Granados
stops.tips: 1730 tunnels beneath a restored mansion; visit by guided tour.

backups.name: La Brigada San Telmo
backups.tips: A parrilla (steakhouse) with football decor, where the meat is cut with a spoon.

backups.name: Museo Histórico Nacional
backups.tips: National history in Parque Lezama; free. An alternative to Zanjón.

stops.name: Recoleta Cemetery
stops.tips: A city of marble mausoleums with Evita's tomb (Duarte) and plenty of cats. Free, though foreigners have needed a 14,000 ARS ticket since 2025.

stops.name: Floralis Genérica
stops.tips: A giant steel flower that opens and closes with the sun; at Plaza Naciones Unidas.

stops.name: MALBA
stops.tips: Latin American art, including Frida Kahlo and Berni. Discounted entry on Wednesdays.

stops.name: Bosques de Palermo & Rosedal
stops.tips: A rose garden and lakes; rent a rowing boat or a bike.

stops.name: Don Julio
stops.tips: Billed as the world's best steakhouse. Without a reservation, join the queue at 18:45 (champagne is on the house). Order the bife de chorizo and a malbec.

backups.name: El Preferido de Palermo
backups.tips: Don Julio's pink sibling, serving milanesa (breaded cutlet) and tapas.

backups.name: Museo Nacional de Bellas Artes
backups.tips: Free entry; Rodin, Monet, in Recoleta.

stops.name: Caminito
stops.tips: Colourful corrugated-iron houses and street tango. Go during the day and don't stray from the main streets.

stops.name: La Bombonera Boca Juniors
stops.tips: Stadium and museum tour; a shrine to Maradona.

stops.name: El Obrero La Boca
stops.tips: A workers' canteen from 1954 serving milanesa and tortilla. Bono has eaten here.

stops.name: Puerto Madero Puente de la Mujer
stops.tips: Calatrava's bridge and the old port, plus the Fragata Sarmiento ship.

stops.name: Reserva Ecológica Costanera Sur
stops.tips: A nature reserve on the Rio de la Plata shore. Come for sunset; choripán stands are outside.

backups.name: Usina del Arte
backups.tips: A concert hall and gallery in a former power station; in La Boca, free.

stops.name: Tren de la Costa Tigre
stops.tips: One hour from Retiro on the Mitre line (the scenic alternative is the Tren de la Costa). Ends at the Tigre pier.

stops.name: Puerto de Frutos
stops.tips: A market at the old fruit port selling wicker, woodwork and mate gourds.

stops.name: Tigre Delta Boat Tour
stops.tips: The channels of the Paraná delta, with floating houses and market boats. The Interisleña public boat is cheap.

stops.name: Museo de Arte Tigre
stops.tips: The 1912 Tigre Club palace, a Belle Époque building on the riverbank.

stops.name: María Luján Tigre
stops.tips: A riverside parrilla with asado and views.

backups.name: Museo del Mate
backups.tips: A mate museum with tastings; in Tigre.

backups.name: Almacén de Ramos Generales Tigre
backups.tips: A former general store turned restaurant; try the picada (sharing platter).

stops.name: Buquebus Colonia Feribotu
stops.tips: A 1 hour 15 minute ferry (bring your passport; about 70,000 ARS return online) to Uruguay.

stops.name: Barrio Histórico Colonia
stops.tips: A UNESCO-listed Portuguese-Spanish town with Calle de los Suspiros and the Portuguese gate.

stops.name: Faro de Colonia
stops.tips: A lighthouse from 1857 with views over the Rio de la Plata (UYU cash).

stops.name: Charco Bistró Colonia
stops.tips: A riverside bistro; try the chivito (Uruguayan steak sandwich). Pay in UYU or USD.

stops.name: Rambla & Plaza Mayor
stops.tips: The waterfront road, with classic cars. Ferries before sunset run between 17:00 and 19:00.

backups.name: Museo Portugués Colonia
backups.tips: A museum of the Portuguese era; an alternative to the lighthouse.

backups.name: El Buen Suspiro Colonia
backups.tips: Wine and picada on Calle de los Suspiros.

stops.name: Palermo Soho Plaza Serrano
stops.tips: Boutiques and murals, with a design market at weekends.

stops.name: La Cabrera Palermo
stops.tips: Parrilla with 15 small side dishes; 40% off during happy hour, 12:00-13:30.

stops.name: Museo Evita
stops.tips: Evita's clothes and life story, in a Palermo mansion.

stops.name: El Ateneo Grand Splendid
stops.tips: A bookshop in a former theatre, often called the world's most beautiful. On Santa Fe.

stops.name: Tango Show El Viejo Almacén
stops.tips: San Telmo's most traditional tango show, with a dinner package; or go to a milonga (La Viruta is cheap).

backups.name: La Viruta Milonga
backups.tips: A milonga (tango dance night) where locals dance; lesson plus night out.

backups.name: Sarkis Palermo
backups.tips: Armenian meze, an alternative to the parrilla; expect a queue.

days.theme: Teatro Colón and a gentle farewell

stops.name: Teatro Colón
stops.tips: An opera house with some of the world's best acoustics. English tours run every hour; don't miss the golden hall.

stops.name: Obelisco & Avenida 9 de Julio
stops.tips: The world's widest avenue and the obelisk, the symbol of Buenos Aires.

stops.name: Confitería La Ideal
stops.tips: A restored café from 1912; medialunas (small croissants) and café con leche for your farewell.

stops.name: Galerías Pacífico
stops.tips: A shopping centre with a frescoed dome; leather souvenirs (Calle Florida).

stops.name: Ezeiza Havalimanı Tienda León
stops.tips: One hour by bus or taxi; farewell.

backups.name: Museo de Arte Decorativo
backups.tips: The Errázuriz palace; an alternative to the Colón.
